page.overview:
Who is Alec?

is the protagonist in Lonely Freddy, the second story in Fazbear Frights 2: Fetch. He is a troubled teenage boy who rebels against what's considered good and enjoys being different from everyone else. As Hazel's, tenth birthday arrives, Alec begins plotting against her to expose his younger sister as the spoiled brat he's certain she is.

Alec is said to be bigger than others his age. He has unruly blond curls, light-green eyes, slightly crooked teeth with braces, and lanky limbs. Alec also has a turned-up nose that he shares with his mother.

Alec enjoys being boundless and living by his own rules, believing that being “bad” is subjective and a construct that can be worked around. He feels that he’s been judged his entire life and prefers his aunt Gigi over his parents since she isn’t constantly trying to “fix” him behind his back, which he finds out through eavesdropping. Alec is deliberate in how he presents himself and uses deflection to hide his true feelings, only showing negative traits and bullying others. This seemingly leads to constant nightmares, which makes him more resentful of others. Only Hazel tends to catch him off-guard, and he is especially mean towards her. Alec coldly dismisses Hazel and constantly tries to find a hidden agenda whenever she tries to get along with him. After seemingly ruining Hazel’s birthday, he breaks down and feels shame.

Alec was born on August 18th, and his named was created as a mixture of "Alexander" and "Eric" as his parents couldn't decide a name. In preschool, Alec realized he was bigger than the other kids and used his height to move to the front of lines with ease. The other kids didn't object to the games he dictated and he never had to look for a seat at the lunch table. One day, Alec's preschool teacher pulled him aside and told him he was a bully, which he assumed was positive and smiled at. His teacher gave him a horrified look and walked away, and the expression haunted Alec as he grew older. Alec eventually concluded that others determination of bad behavior was based on comparison to others, and he tried to find what others considered good and bad.
